note: LIN-3451: Simple Dispatcher is the reference; each row pins sd plus kit and/or harbour (LIN-4384), and a column that differs from sd carries a difference. LIN-4475: `session` is running | finished | stopped | none; the retired `live` is gone. `[done]` is the runner's own post, read by Harbour only, so it has no report row: SD's pinReport asserts both of its readings against one sd value, and they differ on a [done] line. Harbour's reading is pinned in tests/unit/lin-4375-session-pr-wins.test.js. The kit's ledger also has a `lost` state that no session value names: resolveFollowUp refuses it as it refuses none, so the vocabulary leaves it out. LIN-4475 `fold` (W8): per request, the kit transcript fold (runner.mjs transcriptRequestRecords) against Simple Dispatcher's walkRequestRecords. It compares requestId, model, at and the five token fields, in first-seen order, rendered as one JSON array per side: an absent value renders null, a "" stays "", an absent token field is 0. It excludes harness, agent, effort, the skipped counts, and SD's attribution of one request across several transcripts. Its corpus rows name the eight files in tests/fixtures/runner-kit/transcript-corpus by id and sha256; its inline rows carry their own lines.

rows.sd: the agent's request is answered 429; retry-after 1
rows.kit: start fails naming HTTP 429 and Retry-After: 1
rows.difference: LIN-4378: each side answers whoever asked for the exchange. The kit exchanges once in `start`, before the broker serves any agent request, so the runner that called `start` gets the refusal (an error naming HTTP 429 and the wait) and can start again. SD exchanges lazily on the agent's first request, so that request is answered 429 with its Retry-After. Neither turns the 429 into a generic failure.
